items.hackathon: Memory is the obvious moat layer — build a scoped-down version (e.g. memory for one vertical like coding agents) or a novel retrieval strategy on top.
items.innovative: Recall runs four retrieval strategies in parallel (semantic, keyword BM25, graph, temporal), merges them with reciprocal rank fusion, and reranks with a cross-encoder. Separately, a background consolidation turns retained facts into 'observations' — deduplicated, evidence-backed beliefs that are refined rather than overwritten when new evidence arrives — and then into 'mental models' (standing synthesized answers) and knowledge pages. Memories live in isolated 'banks' with tag scoping, and 'Memory Defense' scans retains for secrets/PII. The twist isn't memory itself — it's refine-don't-overwrite consolidation plus 4-strategy fused recall.
items.name: hindsight
items.what: Agent memory that learns — memory infrastructure with integrations for 25+ agent frameworks (LangGraph, Claude Agent SDK, CrewAI, OpenAI Agents). #1 on GitHub weekly trending (+16K stars this week, 44.8K total). Apache-2.0, Docker-first (surrealdb + qdrant + redis).

items.hackathon: Testing that writes itself — agent watches your app, generates tests from a prompt, self-heals flaky selectors.
items.innovative: One framework that mixes deterministic and agentic APIs in the same test — use locators and deterministic assertions where stable, drop in agent steps like agent.act()/agent.assert() for flows you'd otherwise hand-describe; works across web and mobile with the same API. BYO agent/infra: any model via Vercel AI Gateway, or sign in with ChatGPT/GitHub Copilot/SuperGrok subscription. Fully open source, npx e2e init, runs locally or in CI. Novelty is the hybrid deterministic+agentic testing contract rather than pure-agent E2E.
items.name: e2e
items.what: The agentic testing framework for any app (YC P26 TesterArmy, launched Oct 1, 2026, 1.1M views). rauchg: 'The future is verification-engineering. Some tests will be written by hand, most will be generated by AI and executed on real browsers.'

items.name: MCP security scanner (life-forge)
items.what: Deterministic static scanner for MCP tool definitions (Show HN, Oct 3, 2026): flags schema poisoning, invisible/bidi Unicode, homoglyph tool-name spoofing, destructive tools with no authorization surface, unbounded params, cross-server tool shadowing, and rug-pull description drift.
items.innovative: Treats MCP tool definitions as an attack surface with deterministic checks rather than asking an LLM to judge safety — its scan of 15 popular public MCP servers rated 40% CRITICAL.
items.hackathon: An "is my agent's MCP stack pwned?" audit tool — a perfect pre-flight check for any agent hackathon build.

items.name: hyperframes
items.what: "Write HTML. Render video. Built for agents." Open-source rendering layer (HeyGen team, a small startup) letting AI agents generate videos by writing plain HTML instead of wrangling video codecs. Commits 17 minutes before the scan, Oct 3, 2026.
items.innovative: Flips video generation from a codec problem to a document problem — agents already write great HTML, so the renderer meets them where they are instead of teaching them ffmpeg.
items.hackathon: Agents producing explainer videos or ads from a single prompt makes a strong demo.

items.name: raid (offense-research)
items.what: Brand-new Go policy-and-approval engine for AI agents (v0.1.0, Oct 3, 2026): deterministic CEL policies combined with signed, single-use human approvals for agent actions.
items.innovative: Governance built for autonomous agents rather than bolted on — deterministic policy checks gate the action, and human approval is a cryptographically signed single-use token, not a chat interruption.
items.hackathon: Weekend-scale codebase itself; extend it with a policy for one risky action class (e.g. payments).

items.name: Agent Commons Playground
items.what: A playground (here.now) where AI agents find each other and play — a shared social space built for agents, not humans. HN Oct 4.
items.innovative: Agent-to-agent discovery and interaction as the product itself: a social network / play space for agents with humans as spectators.
items.hackathon: Whimsical indie experiment — a multi-agent "town square" with agent-vs-agent games is a great hackathon stage piece.

items.name: impeccable
items.what: "The design language that makes your AI harness better at design" — a design skill for AI coding agents with 24 commands and a shared vocabulary between human and agent. Solo-led indie (pbakaus), 76k stars, commits 6-7 hours ago.
items.innovative: 61 deterministic detector rules compiled into a self-contained Rust engine binary, so design checks run with zero LLM tokens — wired into 17+ agent harnesses via provider-native hook manifests so checks auto-run on agent Stop; plus durable PRODUCT.md as product truth.
items.hackathon: A weekend builder could ship a mini deterministic linter-skill for one niche (e.g. landing-page hero sections) with a small rule set and one harness hook.
